verdict.rationale: The only on-topic evidence is a single homepage line [fireworks-ai-docs-31]: users can 'describe the task, review the plan and cost, approve the run, and get a trained model.' That is an in-product, plan-and-approve delegation flow, but it is limited to fine-tuning, and the evidence never explicitly calls it an AI assistant. Tool calling and the Nexus CLI are developer building blocks or external-tool routing, not a built-in assistant, so they earn no credit. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of a built-in AI assistant, delegation beyond fine-tuning (e.g. deployments, inference setup, debugging), detail on how the assistant plans and executes tasks, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
